The Covariance Blocks That a Summary Prints Ahead of the Equations

Source: R/inference.R
summary_class_blocks.Rd

Returns one block record per covariance class shared by more than one member: the standard deviations and correlations of the shared prior, in which each coordinate is named for the equation, the term and the column to which it belongs.

Usage

summary_class_blocks(
  spec,
  design,
  tables,
  edf = NULL,
  coef = NULL,
  hyper = NULL,
  expected = TRUE,
  emethod = NULL
)

Arguments

spec

A StatmodSpec().

design

The design.

tables

The per-parameter block lists.

edf

The per-term degrees of freedom, or NULL.

coef

The coefficients, or NULL. With hyper, they let the block report what the class itself spends rather than what its members' terms do.

hyper

The hyperparameters, or NULL.

expected

Whether the smoother of a class is read on the expected information. It is the information on which the table edf was read, so that the count of a class and the counts of its members are shares of the same matrix.

emethod

The method that obtains the expected information, as for statmod_edf().

Value

A list of block records in the shape that print_block() reads. Each record carries its coordinates in coords. The list is empty where every class has fewer than two members.

Details

A shared block belongs to no single member. Printed inside the block of one member, it would report the standard deviation of an effect on sigma under a term of mu, and the block of the other member would state that there is nothing to report on its own. The block is therefore printed once, before the equations, where its coordinates can be given names.

The rows are those that summary_blocks() held apart, so the numbers are produced in one place; this function adds the heading of the class and the legend that gives the term of each coordinate.

See also

class_coords() for the naming, class_notes() for the note that gives the same information in prose.
